text:
mike: FYI customer ACME reporting NXDOMAIN for their private inference endpoint (inference-api.acme.internal) after the resolver changes earlier today. App pods throwing 502s and backend TLS handshake failures. Started ~09:12 UTC.

sara: can you paste the error + a dig from a pod/node? also which VPC/hosted zone are we talking about?

mike: quick dig from a node in vpc-0abc1234:
```
$ dig +short inference-api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> +short inference-api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
and from /etc/resolv.conf we forward to the VPC resolver (10.0.0.2). pods get NXDOMAIN when resolving via kube-dns too.

carlos: last change was the Route53 resolver rule update around 08:50 (changed the forwarder IP). could be a hosted zone VPC dissociation too. do `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z123EXAMPLE` for the acme private zone.

mike: ran that, output showed the hosted zone exists but no VPCs listed under the hosted zone:
```
{ "HostedZone": { "Id": "/hostedzone/Z123EXAMPLE", "Name": "acme.internal.", "Config": {}, "ResourceRecordSetCount": 5 }, "VPCs": [] }
```
so looks like the hosted zone got disassociated from the tenant VPC. i suspect a terraform change accidentally removed the association.

diana: if the zone isn't associated with the VPC you'll get NXDOMAIN from the VPC resolver. also check Route53 Resolver rules that forward that domain — if there's an outbound rule with higher priority pointing to wrong IP you'll see timeouts. run: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=DomainName,Values=acme.internal`

mike: list-resolver-rules returned one forwarder rule pointing to 10.10.10.10 (old peered appliance) and its status is READY. i attempted to re-associate hosted zone with: 
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0abc1234
```
command returned success.

infa-bot: deploy-bot rolled forward resolver config at 08:49 UTC (:hammer_and_wrench:).

mike: after re-association, dig from node shows: 
```
$ dig +short inference-api.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
10.20.30.40
```
but pods still see NXDOMAIN occasionally — likely DNS cache on kube-dns/coredns or node-level systemd-resolved. restarting kube-dns pods and clearing node caches should help.

carlos: yep, kube-dns caches negative responses. run `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=kube-dns` to force refresh. also check whether any node-level caching (systemd-resolved) is pointing at the wrong forwarder.

diana: note: we also saw some TLS errors from the client: `x509: certificate is valid for internal-inference.acme.svc, not inference.acme.com` — that's a symptom: the request hit the internal LB (expected) but SNI/public cert mismatch because the public cert was used for the public hostname. make sure clients call the internal host (SNI) or that the LB has certs with both SANs if needed.

mike: fixed steps performed: re-associated hosted zone to vpc-0abc1234, restarted kube-dns, forced node resolver restart on 2 nodes that had old forwarder IP cached. verified: dig returns A record, curl to https://inference-api.acme.internal:443 returns 200 and TLS handshake OK.

diana: can we add a tf guard or policy to prevent accidental disassociation? also add a small monitor that runs dig from a synthetic pod every 5m against the hosted zone.

mike: +1 on TF guard. creating a follow-up ticket to add resolver integration unit test and a pre-apply check to ensure hosted-zone VPC associations aren't removed.

deploy-bot: rollback of resolver-forwarder change completed at 09:35 UTC (:white_check_mark:).

sara: thanks for the quick triage. closing after customer verifies. :thumbsup:

mike: customer confirmed service healthy. adding postmortem notes to the support ticket and closing the Slack thread. :eyes:
